title: Soft Baked Pretzels with Coarse Salt and Mustard
summary: A bread-flour dough sweetened with brown sugar is rolled into ropes and twisted, dipped in a hot bicarbonate of soda bath for the classic crust, brushed with egg, salted and baked, then served warm with yellow mustard.
equipment: stand mixer with dough hook (or large bowl)
2 baking trays lined with baking paper, lightly oiled

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
coarse pretzel salt or coarse sea salt

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Knead the dough until smooth and leave it to double.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Roll ropes, twist into pretzels and chill to firm up.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the oven and bring the soda bath to the boil.

steps.title: Dip
steps.text: Dip each pretzel 30 seconds, flipping once.

steps.title: Glaze and salt
steps.text: Brush with egg and scatter with coarse salt.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake until deep brown and serve warm with mustard.

tips: Chilling the shaped pretzels makes them much easier to lift into the bath.
Add the bicarbonate of soda slowly; it foams up fast.
Salt the pretzels just before baking or the salt will dissolve.
storage: Pretzels are best warm on the day. Keep leftovers loosely covered at room temperature for 1 day, or freeze unsalted for up to 1 month and reheat in a hot oven. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
